A_target.statement:
Let $R$ be a [[Definition:Commutative Ring with Unity|commutative ring with unity]] and $I$ an [[Definition:Ideal of Ring|ideal]].
Then:
:$\map {\operatorname {Spec} } {R / I} \cong \set {\mathfrak p \in \map {\operatorname {Spec} } R: I \subseteq \mathfrak p}$

B_source.statement:
Let $\pi: R \to S$ be a [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] [[Definition:Ring Homomorphism|ring homomorphism]] with kernel $K$.
Then the ideals of $S$ correspond bijectively to the ideals of $R$ containing $K$.

substitutions.the surjection: the quotient map from the ring onto the ring modulo the ideal
substitutions.the subobjects being matched: the ideals of each ring, restricted to the prime ones

derived.the inclusion-preserving bijection on su: ideals of the quotient correspond to ideals containing the collapsed ideal
derived.primeness on both sides: the correspondence restricts to prime ideals, since the quotients agree

validity_conditions: Taking preimages and images under a surjection gives mutually inverse maps between ideals of the quotient and ideals of the source containing the kernel.
Primeness is preserved in both directions because the corresponding quotient rings are isomorphic, so one is a domain exactly when the other is.
The correspondence preserves inclusion, so it is an isomorphism of the ordered sets of ideals and hence a homeomorphism of the associated spectra.
proof_plan: Let $\pi: R \to R / I$ be the [[Definition:Quotient Ring Epimorphism|quotient map]].
Send an ideal $J$ of $R / I$ to $\map {\pi^{-1} } J$, which contains $I$.

Conversely send $\mathfrak a \supseteq I$ to $\map \pi {\mathfrak a}$.
As $\pi$ is surjective, $\map \pi {\map {\pi^{-1} } J} = J$, and $\map {\pi^{-1} } {\map \pi {\mathfrak a} } = \mathfrak a + I = \mathfrak a$.
Both assignments preserve inclusion, by the [[Correspondence Theorem for Quotient Rings]].

By the [[Third Isomorphism Theorem for Rings]]:
:$\paren {R / I} / \paren {\mathfrak p / I} \cong R / \mathfrak p$
so $\mathfrak p / I$ is [[Definition:Prime Ideal of Ring|prime]] {{iff}} $\mathfrak p$ is prime.
Restricting to primes gives the result.
{{qed}}
